name: Agreement of November 12, 1889 with the Bois Forte and Deer Creek Chippewa under the Nelson Act
citation: Act of January 14, 1889, 25 Stat. 642; agreement in H.R. Ex. Doc. 247, 51st Cong., 1st sess.
nations: Bois Forte Band of Chippewa (Minnesota Chippewa Tribe)
promises: Royce records that the Bois Forte and Deer Creek Chippewa ceded all their title to the Bois Forte and Deer Creek reservations, and their rights in the part of the Red Lake reservation not needed for allotment.

The Court of Claims records that section 7 of the 1889 act placed the money from disposing of the ceded lands in a permanent fund for all the Chippewa in Minnesota, drawing 5 percent interest for fifty years.
The Court of Claims records that the act allowed any Indian to decline removal and take an allotment on the reservation where he lived.
today: Court of Claims suits by the Chippewa Indians of Minnesota under the 1889 act were dismissed in 1938 and 1940; in 1940 the court found a violation of the act in the estimating and sale of pine timber lands but dismissed the petition because offsets exceeded the loss.

openQuestions: In 91 Ct. Cl. 97 (1940) the Court of Claims held that the United States violated sections 4 and 5 of the 1889 act and the agreements under it in estimating and selling ceded pine lands (65,038.33 acres sold July to October 1896), with a loss of at least $340,061.66, but dismissed the petition because offsets exceeded the recovery. The opinion does not name the reservations, and its findings of fact are blacked out in the Caselaw Access Project scan. If the tracts can be placed on Bois Forte or Deer Creek land, this record would be broken.
The Minnesota Chippewa Tribe's Nelson Act claims before the Indian Claims Commission (transferred to the Court of Claims in 1976) were not read for this record.
The Bois Forte Band's history page does not discuss the Nelson Act.

Audit 2026-11-08: the court relied on the re-examination by Inspector J. George Wright and quoted the Commissioner of Indian Affairs calling the estimates "totally unreliable and very much to the disadvantage of the Indians". Wright's report and that letter (S. Doc. 85, 55th Cong., 1st sess., 1897) concern pine lands on the ceded part of the Red Lake Reservation (his field work was at Red Lake, Ts. 149 and 150), not the Bois Forte or Deer Creek reservations. Nothing found places the 1896 tracts on Royce areas 483 or 484, so the status stays no-breach-found.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Chippewa, Bois Forte and Minnesota Chippewa (Court of Claims index) and 'Bois Forte 1889', 'Nelson Act Chippewa', 'Chippewa January 14 1889' (ICC); nothing new. Docket 18-D (Bois Forte) values the 1866 cession, and the 1981-82 Court of Claims orders in Dockets 19, 188 and 189 (229 Ct. Cl. 666 to 736) rule on accounting exceptions, mostly dismissed as res judicata; none is a finding about Bois Forte land under the 1889 agreement.
